painpoints.title: Are you facing these challenges in traditional manufacturing?
painpoints.q1: Comparing unit prices alone, while ignoring the comprehensive cost of tooling, inventory, and failure combined?
painpoints.a1: Traditional tooling often costs hundreds of thousands, and even minor design tweaks can mean re-cutting or repairing the mold — real timelines often slip due to communication, revisions, or structural compromises. Factor in fixturing, inventory amortization, and rework, and the comprehensive cost is usually far higher than quoted unit prices. Metal 3D printing requires no tooling and offers transparent pricing — a clear advantage in overall cost.
painpoints.q2: Sales forecasts miss, and amortized tooling becomes inventory burden?
painpoints.a2: Sales forecasts are often wrong — tooling cost gets justified assuming strong demand, but the product may not sell at all, or demand is uncertain. Capital is already committed and lead times are long, leaving you stuck with inventory and tied-up cash. With 3D printing, you produce to actual demand — no more betting on stockpiles.
painpoints.q3: Casting yield issues driving up hidden rework and complaint costs?
painpoints.a3: Even when conventional casting validates at 80% yield, mass production can still produce sand-hole defects — requiring extra manpower and driving up complaint and lost-order risk. SLM metal 3D printing builds layer by layer with controllable internal quality, reducing the hidden cost of defects.
painpoints.q4: Engineers insist it has to be done this way, but experienced machinists say it's impossible?
painpoints.a4: Engineers and designers insist it must be done this way, while shop-floor machinists say it's impossible — traditional cutting tools and fixtures face geometric accessibility limits, and retiring senior machinists leave an experience gap. Metal 3D printing reduces machining constraints to directly realize complex geometries and internal channels, translating CAD designs into physical reality without compromise.
painpoints.summary: No tooling, no compromise — we turn the impossible into market-ready parts. More than 3D printing — the right process, built for you.

about.title: Our Story & Co-Founders
about.t1_desc: Drawing on years of experience in mechanical product engineering and precision manufacturing, the team recognized that additive manufacturing was rewriting industry rules and invested in industrial FDM plastic 3D printing services — helping clients rapidly turn design concepts into physical validation parts, laying the technical foundation for expanding into metal additive manufacturing.
about.t2_desc: As aerospace-led adoption pushed additive manufacturing toward becoming a standard industrial process worldwide, the team committed to metal 3D-printing application design and equipment development — building the core engineering capability behind today's metal AM services.
about.t3_desc: Officially established the additive manufacturing brand AMPINTEC PLUS, integrating metal printing, precision machining, forging, and casting services to deliver a Made-in-Taiwan one-stop design-to-production solution while expanding into international markets.
about.f1_desc: Officially founded the AMPINTEC PLUS brand in 2025, dedicated to driving the commercialization of metal additive manufacturing. Bringing over 10 years of mechanical product engineering and project management experience, he led teams in developing ultra-high-speed equipment. He represents one of the few global cases of applying metal 3D printing to ultra-high-speed rotating equipment, helping clients reduce carbon emissions by 20%, and redesigned production fasteners via additive manufacturing to boost product line maintenance efficiency by 200%.
about.f2_desc: Co-founded AMPINTEC PLUS in 2025, responsible for integrating traditional manufacturing processes and international business development. Bringing cross-border experience from automotive automation projects in North Africa and tooling production lines in China and Southeast Asia, he previously served as a Senior Mechanical Engineer at a top-three global server and laptop ODM, specializing in precision manufacturing and supply chain management.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What is your Minimum Order Quantity (MOQ)?
faq.a1: 3D printing is free from tooling constraints, allowing production starting from a single unit. We evaluate pricing based on part complexity, volume, and selected materials, ideal for prototyping or low-volume custom production.
faq.q2: What is the typical lead time?
faq.a2: Lead time from 7 days. For production, lead times depend on quantity, printer scheduling, and post-processing needs (e.g., CNC machining, heat treatment, polishing). A detailed schedule will be provided before placing an order.
faq.q3: What file formats do you accept?
faq.a3: We recommend standard 3D CAD formats like STEP (.step / .stp) or IGES (.igs). If you only have 2D drawings, we can also assist in feasibility analysis and conversion.
faq.q4: Is my design data kept confidential?
faq.a4: Yes. All our printing and processing are conducted in Taiwan under strict intellectual property laws. We are fully prepared to sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) before receiving your drawings.
faq.q5: Do you accept small-batch custom or trial orders?
faq.a5: Absolutely, this is one of our core advantages. AMPINTEC PLUS is tailored for R&D validation, low-to-medium volume custom production, mass production demands, and high-precision aerospace or semiconductor parts.

industriesPage.title: Industries
industriesPage.intro: Metal 3D printing fits precision part manufacturing and prototyping needs across many industries. Key application areas are outlined below.
industriesPage.aerospace_desc: Metal 3D printing enables aerospace components with complex internal channels and lightweight structures, paired with machining and polishing for precision dimensions and surface finish — suitable for prototype validation, small-batch parts, and maintenance spares.
industriesPage.semiconductor_desc: Semiconductor production lines often require custom fixtures, transport components, and precision structural parts. Metal 3D printing enables rapid prototyping and small-batch production directly from design files, shortening the wait for equipment adjustments and replacement parts.
industriesPage.mold_desc: Metal 3D printing can produce tooling components and jigs with complex internal channels or lightweight structures, used for production-line support and prototype validation, helping shorten development and testing time.
industriesPage.industrial_desc: Structural parts, brackets, and functional components on industrial equipment lines can be rapidly remanufactured or customized via metal 3D printing based on existing designs, supporting equipment maintenance and line upgrades.
industriesPage.medical_desc: Metal 3D printing can be applied to non-invasive external structural components and surgical assistance tools for medical devices, such as instrument housings and non-implantable assistive jigs, produced in small batches to custom specifications.
industriesPage.trends_disclaimer: Public industry information for technology context only. Not manufactured by AMPINTEC PLUS; no affiliation or supply relationship is implied.
